summary: Implemented provider-neutral, postcondition-based reconciliation for the durable ArtworkOperation journal in src/ArrTags/Artwork, following ADR-003, docs/data-model.md section 3.10.4, docs/architecture.md section 9 (crash-consistent publication and restart reconciliation), and Resolved Blocker 2. ArtworkRecoveryDecisions is the pure implementation of the 3.10.4 decision table: Evaluate(operation, state, current, itemAbsent, observedAt) returns a bounded ArtworkRecoveryDecision (NothingToReconcile, Resume, AbortFenced, CompleteAfter, FinalStateDurable, OwnershipLost, OwnershipUnknown, ItemRemoved, or RecoveryBlocked) and performs no I/O or image mutation, with IsFinalStateDurable exposed for the durable-final-state row. ArtworkReconciler is the registered, provider-neutral invocable boundary: it serializes with normal publication through the shared internal ArtworkSubjectGate (moved out of ArtworkPublisher), reads the authoritative PublishedArtworkState and durable ArtworkOperation (quarantining an invalid record rather than replaying it), re-observes the item and active image through IArtworkSourceReader, distinguishes a confirmed missing item (ItemNotFound failure) from an unobservable image, evaluates the table, and delegates execution to ArtworkPublisher.ExecuteRecoveryAsync; an unexpected failure is contained and never escapes as an exception. ArtworkPublisher now executes the deterministic protocol from a durable operation via a shared recoverable path (ExecutePublicationAsync) used by both the normal publication route and reconciliation, so the supported SaveImage, the durable phase ordering, the readback, and the final PublishedArtworkState commit are never reimplemented. Resume/retry is permitted only when the generation and lifecycle fence allow it (a disable/uninstall/item-removal fence whose before identity still matches aborts a prepared publication with AbortFenced) and the publisher reads the retained derived artifact instead of recapturing the active image; before identity is re-read and revalidated immediately before mutation. An after-identity match (recorded observedAfterIdentity or the validated candidate after content hash) ensures the normal item update is persisted and commits the intended target state. An observable mismatch records OwnershipLost and aborts; an unobservable image records OwnershipUnknown and leaves the image untouched; a confirmed missing item writes an ItemRemoved tombstone and performs no image mutation; a durable final state completes the journal without a further mutation; and an invalid state, operation, or missing/corrupt required artifact enters RecoveryBlocked with no replay or cleanup. No artifact is ever deleted, so an artifact not proven non-active is retained. A previously RecoveryBlocked operation is reconciled by superseding it with the next generation (the store refuses advancing a terminal phase in place), and a decision that remains blocked leaves it RecoveryBlocked for a later reconciliation. ArtworkOperation gained the required candidatePublicationFingerprint and rendererVersion fields so an after-match recovery commits the target state without re-rendering or misattributing the renderer version; both are required for a publication and forbidden for a restoration (docs/data-model.md section 3.10.3 records them). Restoration resume is reported as Deferred and left in place because the guarded restoration mutation is the lifecycle task 5.9; the reconciler still handles restoration after-match completion, ownership loss/uncertainty, item-removal tombstones, and durable-final-state completion. ArtworkReconciler is registered with the existing lazy factory pattern and adds no startup work; no event, queue, library-scan, or library-event wiring was added (Phase 6). New tests in ArtworkReconcilerTests (24 cases) cover every decision branch, the lifecycle-fence abort, before-identity revalidation on resume, repeat-publication source/ownership-token reuse, source-artifact retention (no recapture), corrupt state and operation records, missing derived/source artifacts entering RecoveryBlocked, the item-absent tombstone with no mutation, the durable-final-state completion, resolution of a previously RecoveryBlocked operation, restoration resume deferral, no-op for terminal/absent operations, cancellation, containment of a reader exception, DI registration, and boundary-neutrality. No ADR, RenderVersion, renderer behavior, MediaBrowser.* reference, lock file, or existing passing behavior was changed.

known_limitations: Guarded restoration mutation execution is out of task 5.7 scope (task 5.9 owns disable/uninstall drain and guarded restoration). The reconciler still handles a restoration operation's after-match completion, ownership loss/uncertainty, item-removal tombstone, and durable-final-state completion, but a restoration resume (before identity matches) is reported as Deferred and the operation is left in place for the lifecycle task; no image-removal primitive was added to IArtworkImageWriter.

Reconciliation performs no artifact cleanup at all. This is the fail-closed interpretation of 'cleanup may remove only artifacts proven not to be the active image': an artifact that is not proven non-active is retained. No temporary/staged-artifact cleanup API exists in the current SourceArtifactStore, so the FinalStateDurable safe-cleanup step is a no-op.

No event, queue, hosted-lifecycle startup scan, scheduled reconciliation, or library-event wiring was added; ArtworkReconciler is an invocable boundary only, and Phase 6 drives it. The publisher's normal PublishAsync still refuses new work when a non-terminal operation exists, so the 'complete before new work' invariant is preserved even if a caller forgets to reconcile (it fails closed rather than accepting the work).

A terminal RecoveryBlocked operation cannot be advanced in place because ArtworkOperationPhases treats it as terminal (task 5.6 behavior, asserted by existing tests). Reconciliation resolves it by writing the resolution at the next generation, which the store's generation fence permits; this changes the durable operation's generation while retaining its operation id and intent. A reconciliation that remains blocked rewrites RecoveryBlocked only when the generation must change and otherwise leaves the record unchanged to avoid unbounded generation growth.

The candidatePublicationFingerprint and rendererVersion fields were added to ArtworkOperation beyond the flat data-model 3.10.3 field list, because the journal is the only durable source for committing an after-match final state and the publisher never recorded them before. docs/data-model.md section 3.10.3 was updated to record them; both are required for a publication and forbidden for a restoration. No ADR was changed.

Reconciliation reads the single durable operation for the subject while holding the shared per-subject gate, so the store's single-record generation fence plus the gate ensure the reconciled operation is the current generation; no separate generation token is carried into the decision. The generation/fence enforcement is therefore tested at the lifecycle-fence boundary (AbortFenced) and at the store's existing generation fence.

No live-host, native-Skia, or package-content validation was performed for this task because it performs no image or host work; the environment-guarded Skia/host/package tests remain skipped under the default run exactly as before.
